clue.text: After tea one has little energy: carriage required

parts.note: post- is a prefix meaning after
cha is slang for tea
the Roman numeral for one is I
's is the short form of has, as in 'she's got'
E is the physics symbol for energy, a little of the word

explanation.surface: A tired tea-drinker finds their energy flagging and calls for a ride home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one has' reads as I'S, one letter for each word.
explanation.definitionFit: A post-chaise was a hired horse-drawn travelling carriage of the 18th century.

clue.text: Homes with power plugs

parts.note: a plug is a piece of advertising, so plugs are ads

explanation.surface: Houses fitted with sockets and plugs for electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: Pad is informal slang for a person's flat or home.

clue.text: Order us to rise up, fighting

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising up means the letters are read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A rallying call ordering the people to revolt and fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' is the Order of Merit (OM), not a command; with US it is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumo is a form of Japanese wrestling, so the answer names a kind of fighting.

clue.text: Trickster gets financial penalty intended to avoid a period in jail

parts.note: a con man or con is a trickster
a fine is a money penalty

indicators.note: to avoid says the following word a is left out of the synonym

parts.note: meant is a synonym for intended

explanation.surface: A con artist is fined in the hope of keeping him out of prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to avoid a' removes A from MEANT, leaving MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Confinement is imprisonment, a spell locked up.

clue.text: Gathered a boat is moored in a stretch of water off Perpignan

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a boat moored in water sits inside it, so these letters go within the sea's abbreviation

parts.note: Perpignan is on France's Mediterranean coast; Med is the short name for that sea
taken as written
SS is steamship, a boat

explanation.surface: A boat assembled with others at anchor in the Mediterranean near Perpignan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is moored in' is the container signal; the clue's two 'a's do separate jobs, one going inside the sea, the other leading.
explanation.definitionFit: Amassed means accumulated or collected together, the same as gathered.

clue.text: Comedian's rise?

parts.note: a comic who performs alone at a microphone is a ..., and to rise to one's feet is to ...

explanation.surface: A question about how a comic's career takes off.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'rise' is getting to one's feet, and the same words name a kind of comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-up comic performs on their feet, and to get to your feet is to stand up.

clue.text: Woman from field hospital

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow or field
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A woman who has come from a field hospital, perhaps a nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: Leah is a woman's name, borne by Jacob's first wife in Genesis.

clue.text: Top job in transformed Irish depot

indicators.note: transformed says the letters of the two words are made into something new

explanation.surface: A senior post at an Irish depot that has been revamped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' rearranges IRISH DEPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The editor holds the senior post on a newspaper, so editorship is a top job.

clue.text: Bird I spy at last in warmer surroundings

indicators.note: the heater forms surroundings, holding the other letters within it

parts.note: a heater is something that warms
I as a numeral is one

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of spy

explanation.surface: A bird-spotter, playing I-spy, finally sees one warming itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surroundings' makes the warmer the container; 'I' is read as the number one, and 'at last' takes only the final letter of 'spy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Honeyeaters are an Australasian family of nectar-feeding songbirds.

clue.text: Evil murderer repulsed almost everyone joining protest

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

indicators.note: repulsed, driven back, says the murderer's name is read backwards

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis

indicators.note: almost says the last letter of the word for everyone is cut

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A wicked killer is beaten back as nearly the whole crowd joins a demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repulsed' turns CAIN into NIAC; 'almost' trims ALL to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Demoniacal means devilish, like a demon, so it is a synonym for wicked.

clue.text: Uttered unkind expression

indicators.note: uttered says the word for unkind is said out loud, and a word with the same sound is entered

parts.note: mean is a synonym for unkind

explanation.surface: Someone said something with a nasty look on their face.
explanation.definitionFit: Mien is a person's look or bearing, their facial expression.

clue.text: Secret account of home team's right-winger

parts.note: in means at home
a side is a team, so team's is side's
a Tory is a British Conservative, a right-winger

explanation.surface: A confidential report on the home side's conservative winger.
explanation.walkthrough: The football picture of a home team and a winger hides the politics: TORY is the UK Conservative Party member.
explanation.definitionFit: An inside story is the confidential, behind-the-scenes version of events.

clue.text: Wasting shillings when in France, Ireland and German capital

parts.note: S was the abbreviation for shillings in old British money
quand is French for when
Erin is a poetic name for Ireland

indicators.note: capital means the first letter of the word German

explanation.surface: Money frittered away on travel in France, Ireland and Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling was a pre-1971 British coin, abbreviated S.
explanation.definitionFit: Squandering is spending money or resources extravagantly, wasting them.

clue.text: Shows old man to front of 'mairie' in French city

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father, one's old man

indicators.note: in says the letters go inside the name of the city

parts.note: Nimes is a city in southern France
taken as written

indicators.note: front of picks the first letter of mairie

explanation.surface: Dad leads the way to the town hall in a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mairie' is French for town hall; 'front of' takes just its first letter, and 'in' places that with 'to' inside the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantomimes are theatrical entertainments staged at Christmas, a kind of show.

clue.text: Rebel, some might say, backs support for owner

indicators.note: the rebel backs, comes after, the support

parts.note: a prop is a support

indicators.note: some might say signals that the word is spoken and a sound-alike spelling is entered

parts.note: a rioter is a rebel

explanation.surface: A rebel supports a property owner from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' means the rebel comes after the support; 'some might say' makes the rebel's word heard, entered with a different spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A proprietor is the legal holder of a business or property.

clue.text: Charlie and Henry into very good book

parts.note: A1 means first-class, very good, written AI

indicators.note: into says the letter for Henry goes inside the other letters

parts.note: a book is a read, as in a good read
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Two chaps, Charlie and Henry, getting absorbed in an excellent novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' is British slang for a fool, not a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlie in British slang is a silly fool, the same as a scatterbrain.

clue.text: American in Paris remade in the old country

indicators.note: in says the American letters go inside the other part
remade says the letters of Paris are made up afresh

explanation.surface: An American in Paris is reborn in his homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remade' scrambles the French capital to PRSIA, and 'in' puts the American abbreviation inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Prussia was a German kingdom and state, abolished in 1947, so a country of the past.

clue.text: Clue: largely unimportant composer

parts.note: a tip is a hint or clue

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: petty means trivial, unimportant

explanation.surface: A self-deprecating crossword comment calling a composer mostly insignificant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' cuts PETTY to PETT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Michael Tippett was an English 20th-century composer.

clue.text: Flog way-out oven in Pakistan

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat or flog them
a door is a way out

explanation.surface: Selling an unusual oven in Pakistan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flog' looks like 'sell' and 'way-out' like 'eccentric'; they are TAN, beat, and DOOR, an exit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tandoor is a clay oven used in Pakistani and Indian cooking.

clue.text: To some extent, American did enjoy book by Voltaire

indicators.note: To some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An American reader partly enjoyed a classic French novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Candide is Voltaire's 1759 satirical novella.

clue.text: Scottish trick has power to wrong-foot

parts.note: can means is able to, has the power to
to trip someone up is to wrong-foot them

explanation.surface: A Scots trick that can throw an opponent off balance.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantrip is a Scots word for a magic spell or mischievous prank.

clue.text: Support 'X' ban initially ignored in refurbished cinema

indicators.note: in says these letters go inside the reworked cinema
refurbished says the letters of cinema are done up in a new order

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten

indicators.note: initially ignored says the first letter of ban is left out

explanation.surface: A renovated cinema drops its early ban on X-rated films.
explanation.walkthrough: 'X' looks like the old adult film rating but is the Roman numeral. 'initially ignored' drops a first letter, and 'refurbished' rearranges the venue to MAINCE, which 'in' wraps around TENAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Maintenance is financial support, as paid to a former spouse.

clue.text: Rail operated on time

parts.note: ran a business means operated it

explanation.surface: A railway service operated punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rail' is not a railway but a verb: to rail is to complain angrily.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to protest furiously, to rant.

clue.text: One's spurned shortened cape

indicators.note: shortened says the words are cut at both ends, leaving a run of letters inside

explanation.surface: Someone rejected and left wearing a cut-down cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' trims the ends of 'One's spurned' to leave the four letters in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A ness is a headland or promontory, a cape, as in Loch Ness's Inverness or Orford Ness.

clue.text: Mounties oddly silent

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters of Mounties

explanation.surface: Canadian mounted police strangely saying nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Mute means unable or unwilling to speak, so quiet.

clue.text: Organise rearrangement of decoration

indicators.note: rearrangement of says the letters of decoration are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Arranging the decorations differently.
explanation.definitionFit: To coordinate is to bring parts together and arrange them, to organise.

clue.text: Mostly confident fellow is to spend time on-line

indicators.note: mostly says the word for confident loses its last letter

parts.note: sure means confident

explanation.surface: A self-assured man is going to pass the hours on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims SURE to SUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To surf the web is to browse internet pages one after another.

clue.text: Promotes professional assistant attached to IT supremo

parts.note: pro is short for professional
PA is a personal assistant
Bill Gates founded Microsoft, the computing giant

explanation.surface: An expert's aide joins a tech tycoon's team.
explanation.definitionFit: To propagate an idea is to spread and advance it, to promote it.
